chapters.title: Chapter 5: Trading Mechanics, Risk and Tax

lessons.title: The Forex Calendar: Trading Hours, RBI Policy, US Fed and Data Releases

children.text: On 16 September 2026, the US Federal Reserve announces its rate decision at 2:00 pm in Washington. In Mumbai, that is 11:30 pm. The onshore rupee market closed six and a half hours earlier, and NSE's cross-currency contracts stopped trading four hours before. Every rupee trader and hedger in India will sleep through the most important currency event of the month and wake up to its result as a gap at 9:00 am. Currency markets move on a calendar, and much of that calendar runs on someone else's clock. This lesson maps the hours, the central bank meetings and the data releases that move the rupee, all converted into Indian time.

body.text: Most big currency moves happen at predictable times: central bank decisions and major data releases. Knowing the calendar in IST will not tell you which way a currency will move, but it tells you when not to be caught with a position you cannot manage.

children.text: The extra evening hours for cross-currency contracts exist so Indian traders can react to European trading and the start of the US session. But even 7:30 pm is before most US central bank announcements. Currency derivatives segments also follow their own holiday list, which is not always the same as the equity market's, so check the exchange's currency holiday calendar before planning around a date.

children.text: India does not change its clocks, but the US does. In 2026, US daylight saving time runs from 8 March to 1 November. During those months, New York is 9 hours 30 minutes behind IST. For the rest of the year, it is 10 hours 30 minutes behind. Every US release shifts one hour later in Indian time when US clocks go back in November.

body.caption: US summer time in 2026: 8 March to 1 November

body.title: The December Fed decision
body.prompt: The FOMC meeting on 8 and 9 December 2026 ends with a statement at 2:00 pm New York time, after US clocks have gone back. How many hours ahead of New York is IST at that point? Enter a decimal.
body.explanation: After 1 November 2026, New York is on standard time, 10 hours 30 minutes behind IST. So 2:00 pm New York on 9 December is 12:30 am IST on 10 December. The October decision, before the clock change, lands at 11:30 pm IST.

children.text: Central Bank Meetings: RBI and the US Fed

markDefs.definition: RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee, which sets the repo rate. It meets six times a year on a calendar published in advance.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the US Federal Reserve's rate-setting body. It meets eight times a year.

children.text: Two meeting calendars matter most for the rupee. RBI's
sets India's repo rate and signals its view on inflation and the rupee. The US
moves the dollar against every currency in the world, and through the dollar index and US yields, it often moves the rupee more than RBI does.

body.caption: RBI MPC meetings, FY 2026-27 (decision on the last day, usually announced around 10:00 am IST)
Remaining FOMC decisions in 2026, converted to IST (statement at 2:00 pm New York time)

body.text: Markets move on surprises, not on news. If economists and futures markets expect a Fed hike and the Fed hikes, the dollar may barely react, because the move was already priced in. If the Fed holds when a hike was expected, or signals more hikes than expected in its projections, the dollar can jump. Before any event, find out what the market expects. The gap between expectation and outcome is what moves prices.

Dates and times known weeks in advance

Only position size and low leverage protect you

body.text: Around big releases, spreads widen and prices can jump several levels in a second. A stop-loss placed a few pips from the market can fill far away from its level, and a position held through an overnight Fed decision can open with a gap in India the next morning. If you are not specifically planning for the event, the safest choice is to be smaller or flat before it.

body.title: The overnight gap
body.prompt: Rhea holds 5 lots of EUR/USD futures on NSE through a US jobs report. EUR/USD closes at 1.1600 when NSE's cross-currency session ends and opens the next trading day at 1.1520, gapping straight through her stop at 1.1545. Her normal planned risk is ₹2,626. Using USD/INR 95.50, what is her actual loss in rupees?
body.explanation: The gap is 1.1600 minus 1.1520 = 80 pips. Loss = 80 × $0.10 × 5 lots = $40. At 95.50: $40 × 95.50 = ₹3,820. That is about 1.45 times her planned ₹2,626 risk, because the stop could only fill at the open. Gaps are why event risk calls for smaller positions, not just stops.

body.title: Where will the gap come from?
body.question: Which event is most likely to show up as a gap in USD/INR at 9:00 am IST the next morning, rather than as a move during Indian trading hours?
options: An RBI policy decision announced at 10:00 am IST
India CPI data released at 4:00 pm IST
A US Fed decision announced at 11:30 pm IST
The FBIL reference rate published at 1:30 pm IST
body.explanation: The Fed decision lands after India's rupee markets have closed. Global markets react overnight, the offshore NDF market reprices, and onshore USD/INR opens at the new level. The other three all happen during or shortly after Indian trading hours, when traders can respond in real time.

body.title: A note for hedgers: do not wait for the event

children.text: Hedgers sometimes delay booking a hedge until after an RBI or Fed decision, hoping to get a better rate. That turns a hedge into a bet on the outcome of the event. If Karthik has a confirmed euro payment next month, the calendar should influence how he hedges, for example by hedging before a big event rather than after it, not whether he hedges. Option premiums also tend to rise before major events because expected volatility is higher, so buying protection early is usually cheaper.

body.title: Rhea plans her week
body.scenario: It is Monday, 14 September 2026. Rhea holds 5 lots of EUR/USD futures, risking about ₹2,626 on the trade. This week, India CPI for August has just been released, US CPI data came out on Friday, the FOMC decision is due on Wednesday, 16 September, and her usual trading window is 9:00 am to 7:30 pm IST on NSE. Futures markets are betting on a Fed hike.
body.prompt: Convert the Fed decision into IST, explain how it relates to her trading hours, and set out what Rhea should do with her position before and after the decision. What should she check about market expectations?
body.modelAnswer:
1. The FOMC statement is at 2:00 pm New York time on 16 September. The US is still on daylight saving time, so that is 11:30 pm IST, with the press conference at midnight.
2. NSE's cross-currency session closes at 7:30 pm IST, four hours earlier. She cannot react on NSE until 9:00 am on 17 September, so any move will reach her as a gap.
3. Before the decision: decide in advance whether she wants to hold through it. If not, close or reduce the position before 7:30 pm on 16 September. If she holds, size down so that a gap of 100 pips or more would still be an acceptable loss, and assume her stop may fill far from its level.
4. Expectations: check what futures markets price for the decision and the Fed's projections, since September is a projection meeting. A hike that is fully expected may move EUR/USD little; a hold or an unexpectedly aggressive signal could move it sharply.
5. After the decision: avoid trading in the first minutes of the Indian open when spreads are wide and prices are still adjusting. Reassess the trade based on the new information, not on whether her position is in profit or loss.

points: Rupee markets and rupee-pair derivatives trade 9:00 am to 5:00 pm IST; NSE's cross-currency contracts trade until 7:30 pm.
The US changes its clocks and India does not. US releases land an hour later in IST after daylight saving ends, which in 2026 is 1 November.
RBI's MPC decides on the last day of six meetings a year, with the next FY27 decisions on 7 October and 4 December 2026.
FOMC statements land at 11:30 pm or 12:30 am IST, after Indian markets close, so their effect usually reaches the rupee as a gap at the next open.
India CPI at 4:00 pm on the 12th, US CPI and jobs data in the Indian evening, and weekly reserves and daily FPI flows are the key scheduled data.
Markets react to surprises versus expectations, not to the news itself.
Reduce or close positions before high-impact events you are not planning for, and hedgers should not delay hedges to bet on an event's outcome.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not investment or trading advice. Meeting dates, release schedules and trading hours are based on published calendars and exchange information as of September 2026 and can change. Confirm current timings with RBI, the Federal Reserve, MoSPI, NSE and BSE. Price moves in the examples are illustrative.
